def-feature-measure-energy:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, let $\mathcal H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be the closure of a nonempty convex open set. Let $R:\mathcal H\to[0,\infty)$ be differentiable, with differential locally Lipschitz on bounded subsets of $\mathcal H$ and bounded on every sublevel set of $R$. Let $\Phi:\Omega\to\mathcal H$ be Fréchet differentiable and let $V:\Omega\to[0,\infty)$ be $\lambda_V$-semiconvex, with the convention that $V(u)-\frac{\lambda_V}{2}|u|^2$ is convex on $\Omega$. For a semiconvex function $f$ on a convex domain $D$ with coefficient $\lambda$, define
$$\partial_\lambda f(u)=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^d:f(v)\ge f(u)+\xi\cdot(v-u)+\tfrac{\lambda}{2}|v-u|^2\text{ for every }v\in D\}.$$
For a locally semiconvex function $g$ on $D$, define its local Fréchet subdifferential by
$$\partial g(u)=\left\{\xi\in\mathbb R^d:\liminf_{\substack{v\to u,\ v\in D\\v\ne u}}\frac{g(v)-g(u)-\xi\cdot(v-u)}{|v-u|}\ge0\right\}.$$
When $g$ is globally $\lambda$-semiconvex, this local subdifferential agrees with the convexified supporting set $\partial_\lambda g(u)$.
For every $r>0$, require a nonempty closed convex set $Q_r\subseteq\Omega$, nested increasingly in $r$, such that
$$\{u\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(u,Q_r)\le r'\}\subseteq Q_{r+r'}\qquad(r,r'>0),$$
such that $\Phi$ and $V$ are bounded on $Q_r$, $d\Phi$ is Lipschitz on $Q_r$, and there are fixed constants $C_1,C_2>0$ with
$$\sup_{u\in Q_r}\bigl(\|d\Phi_u\|+\|\partial V(u)\|\bigr)\le C_1+C_2r.$$
Here $\partial V(u)=\partial_{\lambda_V}V(u)$ is the supporting set on $\Omega$, and in the growth bound $\|\partial V(u)\|$ means its minimum element norm, equivalently the bound requires a supporting vector of norm at most $C_1+C_2r$ at every $u\in Q_r$. No bound is imposed on the domain normal cone. The source Assumptions 2.1 use the stronger maximal bound for the ambient potential subgradients before adding the domain indicator; that original bound implies the bounded-selection condition used here. Taking a supremum over the relative-domain supporting set would instead include unbounded normal vectors at proper-domain boundaries and would incorrectly exclude the constrained branch. All original source hypotheses and conclusions are retained by this sufficient, weaker growth convention. For a finite nonnegative Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^d$, set
$$F(\mu)=R\!\left(\int_\Omega\Phi(u)\,d\mu(u)\right)+\int_\Omega V(u)\,d\mu(u)$$
when $\mu$ is concentrated on $\Omega$, the Bochner integral exists, and the scalar integral is finite; set $F(\mu)=+\infty$ otherwise. For $\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ with finite $F(\mu)$, write $m_\mu=\int_\Omega\Phi\,d\mu$ and define its first-variation potential on $\Omega$ by
$$F'(\mu)(u)=dR_{m_\mu}[\Phi(u)]+V(u).$$
No convexity of $R$ is required by this definition.
lem-label-l2-space-is-separable-hilbert:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(S,\Sigma,\sigma)$ be any probability space and let $d\ge1$. Set $K=L^2(\sigma;\mathbb R^d)$ be the space of measurable vector fields modulo equality $\sigma$-almost everywhere with finite squared norm. With
$$\langle X,Y\rangle_K=\int_SX(s)\cdot Y(s)\,d\sigma(s),\qquad \|X\|_K^2=\int_S|X(s)|^2\,d\sigma(s),$$
$K$ is a real Hilbert space. If $\Sigma$ is countably generated, then $K$ is separable. In particular this applies to every Borel probability on $S\subseteq\mathbb R^k$ with its relative Borel sigma-algebra, for any $k\ge1$ independent of the output dimension $d$, and to every finite label space. No separability claim is made for an arbitrary probability sigma-algebra.
lem-bochner-time-l2-is-separable-hilbert:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space and $T>0$, and equip $(0,T)$ with its Borel sigma-algebra and Lebesgue measure. Let $Z=L^2((0,T);H)$ consist of strongly measurable $H$-valued functions modulo equality almost everywhere with $\int_0^T\|u(t)\|_H^2\,dt<\infty$. Then
$$\langle u,v\rangle_Z=\int_0^T\langle u(t),v(t)\rangle_H\,dt$$
is a well-defined real inner product and its induced norm is complete. If $D\subset H$ is any countable dense set, the finite-valued step functions with values in $D$ and finitely many rational interval endpoints are dense in $Z$; in particular $Z$ is separable.
lem-hilbert-valued-path-energy-character:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, $T>0$, and $x:[0,T]\to H$ be continuous. For a finite partition $P=(t_i)_{i=0}^N$ with $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, set
$$Q_P(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\frac{\|x(t_{i+1})-x(t_i)\|_H^2}{t_{i+1}-t_i},\qquad C(x)=\sup_P Q_P(x).$$
If $C(x)<\infty$, then there is a strongly measurable $u\in L^2((0,T);H)$ such that $x(t)=x(0)+\int_0^t u(s)\,ds$ for every $t$, $x$ is norm-differentiable almost everywhere with derivative $u$, and
$$\int_0^T\|u(t)\|_H^2\,dt=C(x).$$
def-localized-hilbert-lift:
## Definition

Assume AC. Fix an arbitrary probability label space $(S,\Sigma,\sigma)$ and $r>0$. Let $K=L^2(\sigma;\mathbb R^d)$ with its usual real Hilbert inner product, and let
$$C_r=\{X\in K:X(s)\in Q_r\text{ for }\sigma\text{-almost every }s\}.$$
Define the indicator $\iota_{C_r}$ to be $0$ on $C_r$ and $+\infty$ outside it, and define the localized lifted energy on $K$ by
$$E_r(X)=R\!\left(\int_S\Phi(X(s))\,d\sigma(s)\right)+\int_SV(X(s))\,d\sigma(s)+\iota_{C_r}(X).$$
The first integral is a Bochner integral. The space $K$ is Hilbert for every probability label space and is separable when $\Sigma$ is countably generated. The latter condition holds for finite labels and for Euclidean Borel labels of any dimension, including joint and triple transport-plan labels. For the flow from a law $\mu_0$ the particular choice is $(S,\sigma)=(\Omega,\mu_0)$ and $X_0(s)=s$. Values of representatives on $\sigma$-null sets do not affect $C_r$ or $E_r$.
thm-semiconvex-hilbert-gradient-flow:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space and let $E:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, lower semicontinuous, bounded below, and $\lambda$-convex, meaning
$$E((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)E(x)+tE(y)-\frac{\lambda}{2}t(1-t)\|x-y\|_H^2\quad(0\le t\le1).$$
For $x\in\operatorname{dom}E$, define
$$\partial_\lambda E(x)=\{\xi\in H:E(y)\ge E(x)+\langle\xi,y-x\rangle_H+\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|y-x\|_H^2\text{ for every }y\in H\}.$$
For every $x_0\in\operatorname{dom}E$, there is a unique curve $x:[0,\infty)\to H$ which is absolutely continuous with square-integrable derivative on every bounded interval, satisfies $x(0)=x_0$ and $-\dot x(t)\in\partial_\lambda E(x(t))$ for almost every $t$, and obeys
$$E(x(t))-E(x(s))=-\int_s^t\|\dot x(r)\|_H^2\,dr\quad(0\le s\le t<\infty).$$
For almost every $t$, $-\dot x(t)$ is the unique minimum-norm element of $\partial_\lambda E(x(t))$. For two such curves $x,\widetilde x$ with initial values $x_0,\widetilde x_0$,
$$\|x(t)-\widetilde x(t)\|_H\le e^{-\lambda t}\|x_0-\widetilde x_0\|_H.$$
lem-lifted-energy-lipschitz-gradient:
## Statement

Assume AC and the hypotheses of the feature-measure energy definition. Fix an arbitrary probability label space $(S,\Sigma,\sigma)$, let $K=L^2(\sigma;\mathbb R^d)$, and let $C_r=\{X:X(s)\in Q_r\text{ for }\sigma\text{-almost every }s\}$. Write $A_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|d\Phi\|$, $B_r=\operatorname{Lip}_{Q_r}(d\Phi)$, $M_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|\partial V\|$, and let $L_r$ and $N_r$ be, respectively, a Lipschitz constant and a norm bound for $dR$ on the closed convex hull of $\Phi(Q_r)$. For all $X,Y\in C_r$, the smooth part $G_r(X)=R(\int\Phi(X)d\sigma)$ has the first-order expansion on $C_r$ with gradient $\nabla G_r(X)(s)=d\Phi_{X(s)}^*\nabla R(\int\Phi(X)d\sigma)$, and this gradient is Lipschitz with constant $L_rA_r^2+N_rB_r$. No separability of the label space is required for these estimates. Consequently $E_r(X)=G_r(X)+\int V(X)d\sigma+\iota_{C_r}(X)$ is $(\lambda_V-L_rA_r^2-N_rB_r)$-semiconvex on $K$.
lem-localized-lift-subdifferential:
## Statement

Assume AC and the hypotheses of the feature-measure energy definition. Fix any probability label space $(S,\Sigma,\sigma)$ and use the localized lift $E_r$ on $K=L^2(\sigma;\mathbb R^d)$. Separability of $K$ is not assumed or needed for the subdifferential formula and minimum-section conclusion. For a semiconvex functional $J:K\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ with coefficient $\alpha$, define
$$\partial_\alpha J(X)=\{\eta\in K:J(Y)\ge J(X)+\langle\eta,Y-X\rangle_K+\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\|Y-X\|_K^2\text{ for all }Y\in K\}.$$
The set $C_r$ is closed and convex, and $E_r$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and lower bounded. Write $A_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|d\Phi\|$, $B_r=\operatorname{Lip}_{Q_r}(d\Phi)$, $M_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|\partial V\|$ in the bounded-selection convention, and let $L_r,N_r$ bound the Lipschitz constant and norm of $dR$ on the closed convex hull of $\Phi(Q_r)$. Let $C_r^{\rm sm}=L_rA_r^2+N_rB_r$ and $\lambda_E=\lambda_V-C_r^{\rm sm}$. For $X\in C_r$, its Hilbert subdifferential with coefficient $\lambda_E$ is exactly
$$\partial_{\lambda_E} E_r(X)=\left\{s\mapsto d\Phi_{X(s)}^*\nabla R\!\left(\int\Phi(X)d\sigma\right)+\zeta(s):\ \zeta\in K,\ \zeta(s)\in\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_{Q_r})(X(s))\text{ for }\sigma\text{-almost every }s\right\}.$$
The pointwise minimum-norm selection $u\mapsto\operatorname{argmin}\{|z|:z\in\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_{Q_r})(u)\}$ is Borel on $Q_r$ and has norm at most $M_r$; hence its composition with any $X\in C_r$ is a measurable member of $K$. More generally, for $a\in\mathcal H$ put $b_a(u)=d\Phi_u^*a$ and $S(a,u)=\operatorname{argmin}\{|z|:z\in b_a(u)+\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_{Q_r})(u)\}$. This full shifted minimum is jointly Borel in $(a,u)$, has $|S(a,u)|\le A_r\|a\|+M_r$, and the minimum-norm element of $\partial_{\lambda_E}E_r(X)$ is exactly $s\mapsto S(\nabla R(\int\Phi(X)d\sigma),X(s))$. It is generally different from the smooth gradient plus the minimum of the potential subdifferential alone.
def-generalized-wasserstein-geodesic-and:
## Definition

Assume AC. Let $\mu_0,\mu_1\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$. A generalized $W_2$ geodesic from $\mu_0$ to $\mu_1$ with base $
u\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ is a probability measure $\pi$ on triples $(z,x,y)$ whose $(z,x)$ marginal is an optimal coupling of $
u$ and $\mu_0$ and whose $(z,y)$ marginal is an optimal coupling of $
u$ and $\mu_1$; its interpolating curve is $\mu_t=((1-t)x+ty)_\#\pi$. A functional $F$ is $\lambda$-convex along generalized geodesics if for every such $\pi$ its values satisfy $F(\mu_t)\le(1-t)F(\mu_0)+tF(\mu_1)- rac{\lambda}{2}t(1-t)\int|x-y|^2d\pi$. A vector field $g_\mu\in L^2(\mu;\mathbb R^d)$ is a strong Wasserstein subgradient of $F$ at $\mu$ if for every $\eta\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ and every coupling $\gamma$ of $\mu$ and $\eta$, $F(\eta)\ge F(\mu)+\int g_\mu(x)\cdot(y-x)d\gamma+o\!\left((\int|y-x|^2d\gamma)^{1/2}ight)$ as the coupling action tends to zero, with a remainder uniform over all such couplings. The definition imposes no global displacement-convexity claim.
def-wasserstein-gradient-flow-for-featur:
## Definition

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. For $\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ with finite energy, define $F'(\mu)(u)=dR_{m_\mu}[\Phi(u)]+V(u)$ on $\Omega$, and extend this potential by $+\infty$ off $\Omega$. Its constrained subdifferential at $u$ is the local Fréchet subdifferential of $F'(\mu)+\iota_\Omega$ defined in the feature-measure-energy convention. A Wasserstein gradient flow from $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ is a curve $t\mapsto\mu_t$ in $AC^2_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty);(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d),W_2))$, with $\mu_{t=0}=\mu_0$, for which there is a Borel velocity $v_t(u)$ satisfying the finite-action continuity equation and $v_t(u)$ equals the negative minimum-norm element of $\partial(F'(\mu_t)+\iota_\Omega)(u)$ for $dt\,d\mu_t(u)$-almost every $(t,u)$. This definition does not assert that the energy is displacement convex.
lem-feature-energy-geodesically-semiconv:
## Statement

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Fix $r>0$ and let $\mu_0,\mu_1\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ be concentrated on $Q_r$. Let $\pi$ define any generalized $W_2$ geodesic between them, and put $\mu_t=((1-t)x+ty)_\#\pi$. With $C_r=L_rA_r^2+N_rB_r$, for every $t\in[0,1]$,
$$F(\mu_t)\le(1-t)F(\mu_0)+tF(\mu_1)-\frac{\lambda_V-C_r}{2}t(1-t)\int|x-y|^2d\pi.$$
The cost in this inequality is the cost of the specified plan and need not equal $W_2^2(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ when $\lambda_V-C_r<0$. This does not assert global displacement convexity.
lem-characteristics-unique-and-stable:
## Statement

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Fix $r>0$ and a nonempty closed convex constraint $D\subseteq\Omega$. For every continuous moment path $m:[0,T]\to\mathcal H$, the nonautonomous inclusion
$$\dot X(t)\in-\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_D)(X(t))-d\Phi_{X(t)}^*\nabla R(m(t))$$
has a unique forward solution from each $X(0)\in D\cap Q_r$; its characteristic map is jointly continuous in $(t,X(0))$ and locally Lipschitz in the initial point on each $Q_r$. Let $\mu_t$ and $\nu_t$ be two finite-action solutions on $[0,T]$ of the continuity equation with laws concentrated on $D\cap Q_r$ and velocities
$$v_t^\alpha(x)=-\operatorname{argmin}\{|q|:q\in d\Phi_x^*\nabla R(m_{\alpha_t})+\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_D)(x)\},\qquad\alpha\in\{\mu,\nu\},$$
where $m_\alpha=\int\Phi\,d\alpha$. The full shifted minimum selection is Borel; it need not be continuous in position. Each finite-action PDE solution with a continuous prescribed feature moment is the pushforward by its unique characteristic map. For starts in $D\cap Q_r$, these characteristics remain in a larger $Q_R$ uniformly on compact time intervals, and their velocity is the negative full shifted minimum almost everywhere. The same construction applies directly to any continuous forcing $a(t)\in\mathcal H$ in place of $\nabla R(m(t))$. Then for all $t\in[0,T]$,
$$W_2(\mu_t,\nu_t)\le e^{(C_r-\lambda_V)t}W_2(\mu_0,\nu_0),\qquad C_r=L_rA_r^2+N_rB_r.$$
Here $A_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|d\Phi\|$, $B_r=\operatorname{Lip}_{Q_r}(d\Phi)$, $M_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|\partial V\|$ in the bounded-selection convention, and $L_r,N_r$ are respectively a Lipschitz constant and a norm bound for $dR$ on the closed convex hull of $\Phi(Q_r)$. In particular, the localized measure-valued flow is unique for each initial law. The estimate does not assume that $v_t$ is continuous in position.
lem-w2-distance-derivative-under-a-conti:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $(\mu_t,v_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a narrowly continuous finite-action solution of the continuity equation on $\mathbb R^d$, and fix $
u\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$. For almost every $t\in(0,T)$, the scalar map $t\mapsto rac12W_2^2(\mu_t,
u)$ is differentiable and, for every optimal coupling $\gamma_t$ of $\mu_t$ and $
u$,
$$ rac d{dt} rac12W_2^2(\mu_t,
u)\le\int_{\mathbb R^d	imes\mathbb R^d}(x-y)\cdot v_t(x)\,d\gamma_t(x,y).$$
lem-feature-energy-strong-wasserstein-su:
## Statement

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Fix $r>0$ and $\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ concentrated on $Q_r$. Define $g_\mu(u)=S(\nabla R(\int\Phi\,d\mu),u)$, the minimum-norm element of $d\Phi_u^*\nabla R(\int\Phi\,d\mu)+\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_{Q_r})(u)$. For every $\eta\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ concentrated on $Q_r$ and every coupling $\gamma$ of $\mu$ and $\eta$,
$$F(\eta)\ge F(\mu)+\int g_\mu(x)\cdot(y-x)d\gamma(x,y)+\frac{\lambda_V-C_r}{2}\int|y-x|^2d\gamma(x,y),\qquad C_r=L_rA_r^2+N_rB_r.$$
In particular, $g_\mu$ is a strong Wasserstein subgradient of the localized functional $F_r$, defined as $F$ on laws concentrated on $Q_r$ and $+\infty$ otherwise, in the all-coupling sense, with zero remainder after the stated quadratic term. Here $A_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|d\Phi\|$, $B_r=\operatorname{Lip}_{Q_r}(d\Phi)$, and $L_r,N_r$ are respectively a Lipschitz constant and norm bound for $dR$ on the closed convex hull of $\Phi(Q_r)$; put $\lambda_r=\lambda_V-C_r$. It is the unique minimum-norm vector field among all all-coupling strong subgradients in $L^2(\mu;\mathbb R^d)$.
lem-localized-lift-generates-continuity-:
## Statement

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ have finite energy and be concentrated on $Q_r$, and let $X:[0,\infty)\to K=L^2(\mu_0;\mathbb R^d)$ be the Hilbert gradient flow of the localized lift $E_r$ from $X(0,s)=s$. Define $\mu_t=(X(t,\cdot))_\#\mu_0$, $m_t=\int\Phi(X(t,s))d\mu_0(s)$, and
$$v_t(u)=-S(\nabla R(m_t),u),$$
where $S(a,u)$ is the minimum-norm element of the full shifted set $d\Phi_u^*a+\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_{Q_r})(u)$. Then $v$ is Borel, $\int_0^T\int|v_t|^2d\mu_tdt<\infty$ for each $T<\infty$, and $\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0$ in distributions on $(0,T)\times\mathbb R^d$. The curve $\mu_t$ is in $AC^2([0,T];\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d),W_2)$, and $v$ is the minimum-action velocity, satisfying $\int_0^T\int|v_t|^2d\mu_tdt=\int_0^T|\dot\mu_t|_{W_2}^2dt$.
thm-localized-wasserstein-flow:
## Statement

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $r>0$ and let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ have finite energy and be concentrated on $Q_r$. There is a unique curve $\mu:[0,\infty)\to\mathcal P_2(Q_r)$ in $AC^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ that starts at $\mu_0$, solves the continuity equation with velocity equal almost everywhere to the negative minimum-norm element of $\partial(F'(\mu_t)+\iota_{Q_r})$, and satisfies
$$F(\mu_t)-F(\mu_s)=-\int_s^t\int|v_q(u)|^2d\mu_q(u)dq\qquad(0\le s\le t<\infty).$$
Writing $\lambda_r=\lambda_V-L_rA_r^2-N_rB_r$, it also satisfies the evolution variational inequality
$$\frac12\frac d{dt}W_2^2(\mu_t,\eta)+\frac{\lambda_r}{2}W_2^2(\mu_t,\eta)\le F(\eta)-F(\mu_t)$$
for each fixed $\eta\in\mathcal P_2(Q_r)$ and almost every $t>0$ (with the exceptional null set allowed to depend on $\eta$). Any two such localized flows obey $W_2(\mu_t,\nu_t)\le e^{-\lambda_r t}W_2(\mu_0,\nu_0)$.
lem-feature-flow-escape-bound:
## Statement

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $r_0>0$ and let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ have finite energy and be concentrated on $Q_{r_0}$. Set $M_0=\sup\{\|\nabla R(z)\|:R(z)\le F(\mu_0)\}$, $a=(1+M_0)C_1$, and $b=(1+M_0)C_2$. For $T<\infty$, define
$$r(T)=\begin{cases}(r_0+aT),&b=0,\\(r_0+a/b)e^{bT}-a/b,&b>0.\end{cases}$$
For every $R>r(T)$, the localized flow with indicator $\iota_{Q_R}$ remains in $Q_{r(T)}$ for $0\le t\le T$ and therefore solves the continuity equation with the constraint $\Omega$ alone on this interval. Localized flows with different cutoffs larger than $r(T)$ agree on $[0,T]$. In particular no trajectory starting in $Q_{r_0}$ can escape every cutoff in finite time.
thm-global-wasserstein-flow-existence-un:
## Statement

Assume AC and the full feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ have finite energy and be concentrated on $Q_{r_0}$. There is a unique global curve $\mu:[0,\infty)\to\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ in $AC^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $\mu_{t=0}=\mu_0$ that solves the continuity equation with the negative minimum-norm subgradient velocity of the extended potential $F'(\mu_t)+\iota_\Omega$. For every finite $T$, the curve is concentrated on some $Q_{r(T)}$ and satisfies
$$F(\mu_t)-F(\mu_s)=-\int_s^t\int|v_q(u)|^2d\mu_q(u)dq\qquad(0\le s\le t\le T).$$
For any $\mu_0,\nu_0$ concentrated on the same $Q_{r_0}$, their flows obey $\sup_{0\le t\le T}W_2(\mu_t,\nu_t)\le e^{K_TT}W_2(\mu_0,\nu_0)$ for a finite constant $K_T$ depending only on $T$, $r_0$, and a common upper bound for the initial energies. Consequently, W2-convergent initial laws in a common $Q_{r_0}$ have flows converging uniformly in W2 on every compact time interval.
thm-finite-particle-flows-converge-in-w2:
## Statement

Assume AC and the full feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ be concentrated on a common $Q_{r_0}$, and let $\mu_{m,0}=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\delta_{x_i^{(m)}(0)}$ be empirical laws with every particle in $Q_{r_0}$ and $W_2(\mu_{m,0},\mu_0)\to0$. Define $F_m(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=F(m^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i})$. Here $\partial F_m(x)$ is the Euclidean Fréchet subdifferential: $p\in\partial F_m(x)$ when $F_m(y)\ge F_m(x)+p\cdot(y-x)+o(\|y-x\|)$ as $y\to x$ in $\Omega^m$, with the remainder divided by $\|y-x\|$ tending to zero. A classical particle subgradient flow is a locally absolutely continuous vector $x^{(m)}(t)\in\Omega^m$ satisfying $\dot x^{(m)}(t)\in-m\partial F_m(x^{(m)}(t))$ almost everywhere, under the inner product $m^{-1}\sum_i x_i\cdot y_i$. Let $x_i^{(m)}(t)$ be such flows and put $\mu_{m,t}=m^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i^{(m)}(t)}$. If $\mu_t$ is the unique global measure-valued flow from $\mu_0$, then for every $T<\infty$ there is a finite constant $K_T$ independent of $m$ such that
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}W_2(\mu_{m,t},\mu_t)\le e^{K_TT}W_2(\mu_{m,0},\mu_0)\longrightarrow0.$$
This is a deterministic continuity estimate in the initial W2 error; it asserts no statistical rate for random initial particles and no conclusion for stochastic gradient descent.
